The clarinet version of [Patterns by Ear](patterns-by-ear.qmd). The first few patterns of a set are taught with fingering diagrams.
Then the page plays the rest, one at a time, and you play each back on your clarinet. New to the fingerings? See the
[fingering chart](../lessons/clarinet.qmd#fingering-chart).

## How it works {#how}

- **Written notes.** Everything on this page is in *written* pitch, the notes on your part. The page plays them at the
  pitch your clarinet really sounds (B♭ clarinet a major 2nd lower, A a minor 3rd, alto a major 6th, bass a major 9th, and so on),
  and the microphone turns what it hears back into written notes. So pick your clarinet above. The transpositions are not from the book:
  see the [lesson](../lessons/clarinet.qmd#family).
- **Range.** Each set is moved to the written key you pick and placed between written G3 and F5, from the lowest note that needs no
  little-finger key up past the break, when it fits. (A rule of thumb, not checked.) Some patterns cross the break between A♯4 and B4.
- **Fingerings.** The first fingering the book shows for each note, from the [fingering chart](../lessons/clarinet.qmd#fingering-chart). Your teacher may prefer an alternate.
- **What counts.** The notes in order; rhythm isn't checked. Each new note must hold steady for about a tenth of a second. To play the
  same note twice, stop the sound briefly between them (tongue it). With *Any octave counts* on, the whole pattern may be an octave away.
  Stopping for more than four seconds starts the try again.
- **The microphone** ignores everything while the page is playing. Headphones still help: a loud room can confuse it.
- **No clarinet handy?** A MIDI keyboard or wind controller, or the computer keys, count as written notes.

Unverified: the transpositions of the family in the lesson's table (B♭ M2, A m3, E♭ soprano m3 up, alto M6, bass M9, contra-alto octave + M6, contrabass two octaves + M2, basset horn P5), the register names (chalumeau, throat tones, clarion, altissimo) and the tuning advice. Not yet re-read.

**For teachers**

"Clarinet." Teacher resource book, Neil A. Kjos Music Company (item W74; title and authors unverified), pp. 118-39. History (Denner, Müller, Klosé and Buffet), family, selecting players, reeds and reed adjustment, ligatures, parts, assembly, posture, embouchure, care, checklist, tone problems, vibrato, listening list, B♭ clarinet fingering chart (p. 136), trill chart (p. 137), alto / bass / contralto / contrabass chart (p. 138) and its trill chart (p. 139). Retold in the page's own words; charts redrawn from the book's key template. Not in the scanned pages: the tuning chart.
